A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DISC research. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark experiments on APPS, MATH500, and LiveCodeBench, alongside model comparisons, ablations, and decomposition analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains the original benchmark results, model comparisons, ablations, and supplementary empirical analyses.

M1.justification: Prefix proposal, z-score acceptance, contraction, and search integration remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 makes reward statistics explicit through revised sample-set notation, consistent with v2's prose and unchanged appendix implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same APPS, MATH500, and LiveCodeBench coverage, including the APPS setting with self-generated validation tests. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: BoN, TokenSplit, and LineSplit remain the decomposition comparators. The greedy/beam/MCTS comparisons and alternative acceptance rules also retain the same membership.

E3.justification: Dataset subsets, sample budgets, model configurations, and Pass@k/Pass@token metrics are retained. The default partition fraction 0.15, sampling threshold 1.0, and temperature 0.2 are unchanged, as are the appendix-specific settings.

E4.justification: The temperature, acceptance-rule, model, partition-fraction, reward-distribution, search, and decomposition case analyses are retained. The new limitations discussion introduces no additional robustness tests or ablation evidence.

E5.justification: Run/seed disclosure and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged, including the reward standard-deviation analyses. V3's explanation of dotted linear trend lines describes lines already present in v2.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted curves are unchanged, including the reported 5.0%, 6.7%, and 10.5% error reductions. The runtime breakdown moves from v2 Figure 43 to v3 Figure 7, retaining DISC's 9.1% overhead.

T1.justification: The optimality statements, assumptions, lemmas, proofs, and Wiener-process example are retained; v2 Appendix F becomes v3 Appendix G. Algorithm 1's more explicit reward notation does not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive decomposition, search compatibility, inference efficiency, and performance gains.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands applicability and validity qualifications through Sections 4.1/4.3 and new Appendix E. It discusses incomplete or incorrect generated tests, biased evaluation and comparison, reward-model dependence, single-turn scope, and reduced benefits on trivial or non-compositional tasks. These specific limitations were largely absent from v2.

D1.justification: V3 adds a project-website access pointer on the title page. The appendix implementation, hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not establish the linked resources' availability.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds citations to Recursive Inference Scaling and DynScaling, listed as references 54 and 55 in v3. This modestly extends the adaptive-compute context without substantially changing research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites the runtime and self-generated-validation discussion, adds a limitations subsection and appendix, clarifies pseudocode notation, and updates author footnotes and venue text. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 relocates Algorithm 1, exchanges the order of Figures 2 and 3, and moves the runtime chart into the main text. Figure 6 and the decomposition-analysis caption gain explanations. Existing graphics are retained, with limited layout and code-formatting changes.

improvement.justification: V3 improves transparency through concrete limitations concerning reward reliability, generated tests, and applicability. Clearer scoring notation, explanatory captions, and the project access pointer also improve usability. These are focused documentation gains; the empirical evidence and proofs remain unchanged, and the newly discussed test-reliability concerns are not investigated further.
